tested_scope: Constructed role-local scheduled-Chat assignment-switch trace CAN-4 at scope S1 only; this is a controller-mechanism conformance test, not a benchmark of Argo Rollouts, Flagger, Kubernetes, or production deployment quality.

public_sources.name: Argo Rollouts canary documentation
public_sources.bound_semantics: Canary progression is an ordered sequence of steps evaluated before the new ReplicaSet becomes stable; pause/step semantics preserve an old stable version while the rollout progresses.

public_sources.name: Argo Rollouts getting started
public_sources.bound_semantics: After all rollout steps complete, the new ReplicaSet becomes stable; abort during an update falls back to the stable version.

public_sources.name: Flagger deployment strategies
public_sources.bound_semantics: A canary control loop gradually shifts exposure while measuring KPIs and promotes or aborts based on analysis; progressive promotion can occur in stages.

source_binding_limit: Only staged validation, promotion-after-gates, and fallback/abort semantics are imported. External rollout controllers, service meshes, metric backends, Kubernetes clusters, webhooks, hosted observability, and manual promotion are not accepted execution dependencies for this Chat-native reduction.

fatal_gate_results.F1: PASS for CN-C: A remains authoritative until a distinct PROMOTED terminal identity is durably read back; preparation and stage observations do not transfer authority.
fatal_gate_results.F2: PASS for CN-C: accepted route uses only role-local durable repository state plus scheduled Chat reasoning; no richer-mode/manual-user/protected-primary/external hosted rollout controller, finite optional quota, or incremental monetary cost. CN-D fails F2.

candidate_results.reason: Immediate authority transfer after C1 violates G3 and G4 and therefore F1 because promotion occurs before all precommitted gates and before promoted-terminal readback.
Allowing attempted/non-read-back writes or duplicates to satisfy gates violates G2 and G9 and cannot establish a distinct terminal promotion identity.

success_trace: C1 distinct same-scope terminal observation B=8.7 vs A=8.0 passes; durable stage state records C1 PASS; A remains authoritative.
C2 second distinct same-scope terminal observation B=8.8 vs A=8.1 passes; durable stage state records C2 PASS; A remains authoritative.
C3 third distinct same-scope terminal observation B=8.9 vs A=8.0 passes with no guard violation; A still remains authoritative until promotion terminal identity is sealed/read back.
Append CAN-4:PROMOTED and independently read it back; only then transfer current authority to B. A duplicate CAN-4:PROMOTED replay is a no-op and earns no second credit.
failure_trace: C1 B=8.7 vs A=8.0 passes but A remains authoritative.
C2 B=8.2 vs A=8.1 fails the precommitted +0.5 criterion, so CAN-4 becomes ROLLBACK/REJECTED and A remains authoritative.
All prior A/B evidence remains immutable history; rollback is qualification-only and does not destructively undo read-back evidence.
A late stale CAN-4:PROMOTED completion after rejection is rejected and cannot transfer authority.

controls.scope_mismatch_S2: PASS: does not satisfy a stage
controls.transport_timeout: PASS: does not satisfy a stage
controls.duplicate_C1: PASS: does not satisfy the next stage

candidate_results.reason: Delegating rollout, metric collection, and promotion to an external deployment controller is a residual external execution dependency and may also entail finite hosted quotas.

accepted_claim: For the exact constructed CAN-4 role-local trace, durable staged validation plus readback-gated promotion prevents premature assignment authority transfer, preserves old-authority safety on failure, rejects stale late promotion, and is resumable after non-semantic transport failures.
not_claimed: No claim of production rollout safety, statistical superiority, deployment-system equivalence, or general optimizer superiority.
exact_next_action_after_readback: Advance controller credit by one only after independently reading this immutable terminal artifact. Then precommit a non-conflicting crash-consistent switch-recovery leaf before any public semantic read for that leaf.
